directAnswer: Pope Adrian V was Ottobuono Fieschi of Genoa, a nephew of Innocent IV, who was elected on 11 July 1276 and died on 18 August 1276, just over five weeks later. He died before being ordained a priest, consecrated bishop or crowned, and his one notable act was suspending Gregory X's strict conclave law, Ubi periculum.

paras: Ottobuono belonged to the Fieschi, a powerful Genoese family; his uncle was Pope Innocent IV, who made him a cardinal deacon in 1252. His most significant service came in England, where Clement IV sent him as legate from 1265 to 1268 to help restore peace after the conflict between Henry III and the barons led by Simon de Montfort.

At a council in London in 1268 he issued a set of legatine constitutions for the English Church. These decrees on clerical discipline and church administration remained an important part of English canon law throughout the Middle Ages. Among the young men in his household in England was a future pope, Boniface VIII.

After Innocent V died in June 1276, the cardinals met in Rome under pressure from Charles of Anjou, who held authority in the city, and elected Ottobuono in July. Still only a cardinal deacon, he went to Viterbo, where he announced that he would revise Ubi periculum, whose harsh conditions many cardinals disliked, and suspended it in the meantime.

He died at Viterbo on 18 August 1276 and was buried in the church of San Francesco there. Because of his short reign, little else can be said with confidence about his plans. Dante places him in Purgatory among those purging the sin of avarice, a literary judgment rather than a historical record.

keyFacts: Born Ottobuono Fieschi in Genoa; nephew of Pope Innocent IV
Papal legate to England (1265–1268); issued legatine constitutions in 1268
Reigned only from 11 July to 18 August 1276
Suspended Gregory X's conclave law Ubi periculum
Died at Viterbo without being ordained priest or crowned

faqs.question: Was Adrian V ever ordained a priest?
faqs.answer: No. He was a cardinal deacon when elected and died about five weeks later at Viterbo before he could be ordained priest, consecrated bishop or crowned.

faqs.question: What did Adrian V do in England?
faqs.answer: As papal legate from 1265 to 1268 he worked for peace after the Barons' War and issued constitutions at a London council in 1268 that long remained part of English church law.
